records.name: Lakshadweep
records.current_summary:
No Lakshadweep-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file. As a union territory without a full legislature, its recognition policy is set by the central government.

That national framework narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament passed an amendment removing the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricting legal recognition to historically recognised communities and intersex people, and requiring medical certification — critics warn many trans and non-binary people will be excluded, a court-appointed advisory panel asked for withdrawal, protests followed the vote, and presidential assent is pending. Whatever the island's local society, the recognition machinery facing a visitor or resident runs through that national law.

sources.claim: The 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill amends the 2019 law: it removes the right to self-identification, limits legal recognition to historically accepted categories and intersex individuals, and mandates medical certification for identity recognition - HRW calls it a major reversal of the 2014 rights and urges the president not to sign it (articles dated 26 Mar 2026).

Amendment bill approved by both houses (article 2026, awaiting presidential assent): removes the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court 'third gender' ruling; narrows the 2019 definition of transgender person; government says the narrower definition improves welfare delivery, critics warn it excludes trans men, trans women, non-binary and gender-fluid people; mandatory medical certification described as an attack on privacy and dignity.

sources.claim: HRW dispatch (2026-03-26): India's parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill 2026, which removes the right to self-identification affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court judgment, limits legal recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural groups (hijra, kinner) plus intersex individuals — excluding self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people — and mandates medical certification for identity recognition. HRW calls it a major setback that strips thousands of rights and increases risk. As national law it sets the recognition baseline for visitors and residents across every Indian state and union territory, including this one.

BBC News (2026-03-26): parliament approved in both houses an amendment to the 2019 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act that redefines transgender identity and removes the self-identification right; it awaits presidential assent. Opposition parties and the LGBTQ community protested; the government says the change makes welfare benefits more accessible, while critics say it excludes transgender, non-binary and gender-fluid people. The piece recalls the 2014 Supreme Court 'third gender' ruling and reports recognition remains uneven amid continuing discrimination in education, healthcare and formal employment — the national baseline that applies in this region.

records.name: Sikkim
records.current_summary:
No Sikkim-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file; the state sits under the national framework, which narrowed sharply in March 2026: parliament removed the self-identification right affirmed by the 2014 Supreme Court ruling, restricted recognition to intersex variations and traditional community identities certified by medical boards, and made board certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. A court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, prominent trans activists warned of mass exclusion, protests followed the vote, and presidential assent is pending.

The framework's enforcement texture nationally includes transit-space 'gender checks': an August 2024 case at a northern railway station, in which a trans traveller alleged a rail-police constable groped her while checking her gender — police denied it and filed a counter-complaint — evidences a policing habit of treating trans appearance as suspicion in federally-policed transit spaces rather than in this state specifically.
records.current_localsOnly: Among the 19 states/UTs that have not constituted the transgender welfare board mandated by the 2020 Rules — a documentation/service-delivery gap for residents rather than a visitor-facing signal.

records.name: Odisha
records.current_summary:
